newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday on an uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,020 yuan ($364) per tonne, down 40 yuan. It opened at 3,090 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,099 and a low of 3,006.
March fell 15 to 3,020, May rose 10 to 3,100, July 20 to 3,120 and September 10 to 3,179 and November dropped four to 3,226.
Combined volume rose to 14,000 tonnes from 12,700.
Traders said long liquidation pushed the January contract down while other contracts moved in a narrow range for most of the session.

"Many investors continued to offset their long positions with the approach of the delivery day of the January contract," one trader said. "Soybean needed a rest after sharp falls over the past few days," he added.
Analysts expect soybean to move in a narrow range in slow trading in the short term.
